existing_capabilities: credfree SMB2 NEGOTIATE probe (dialects 0x0202..0x0302; deliberately excludes 0x0311 to sidestep negotiate-context requirements)
credfree SMB1 NEGOTIATE probe (detects legacy protocol answered)
signing posture split into SIGN_ENABLED (0x01) vs SIGN_REQUIRED (0x02)
shells out to nxc/netexec for null/guest/creds enumeration (shares, users, pass-pol)
enum_best_session ladder: null -> guest -> creds fallback for locked-down hosts
share spidering via smbclient recursive ls with pattern-based secret file flagging (unattend.xml, GPP Groups.xml, web.config, KeePass, private keys, dotfiles, backups)
reversible writable-share proof (put/list/del + explicit cleanup) with put-line-based verdict to avoid false negatives from create-not-delete shares
null_session_findings and readable_share findings from parsed nxc output
credfree/credentialed runbook builders (nmap NSE, enum4linux-ng, nxc, secretsdump, ntlmrelayx)
proof_html reuse from mssql for terminal-transcript screenshots
findings_to_vulns folding into main severity totals + SMB workbook tab

missing_capabilities.name: SMB2 SESSION_SETUP NTLMSSP CHALLENGE harvest
missing_capabilities.description: The probe stops at NEGOTIATE. A follow-up SESSION_SETUP carrying an NTLMSSP NEGOTIATE_MESSAGE (MS-NLMP 2.2.1.1) forces the server to return an NTLMSSP CHALLENGE_MESSAGE (MS-NLMP 2.2.1.2) whose TargetInfo AV_PAIR list (MsvAvNbComputerName, MsvAvNbDomainName, MsvAvDnsComputerName, MsvAvDnsDomainName, MsvAvDnsTreeName, MsvAvTimestamp) plus the Version field (ProductMajor/Minor/Build, NTLMRevision) leak the machine's NetBIOS name, primary domain, DNS FQDN, AD tree name, exact OS build, and server clock -- all pre-auth, stdlib, no creds. This is the highest-value info-disclosure that SMB gives away and the module currently gets none of it.

missing_capabilities.name: Cross-service wiring: known_users / known_hostnames / known_domains / relay_targets feed
missing_capabilities.description: creds/known_users.py, core/known_domains.py, and the relay_targets pattern used by mssql/vault all exist and explicitly cite SMB as a source, but smb.py does not populate any of them. SAMR user list, CHALLENGE hostnames/domains, and every signing_required=False target should be exported so ldap/mssql/vsphere/ntlmrelayx planning consumes them. The module is a producer of cross-service intel that today drops that intel on the floor.

missing_capabilities.name: CVE-2020-0796 SMBGhost detection (SMB 3.1.1 compression)
missing_capabilities.description: The probe explicitly refuses to offer dialect 0x0311, so SMBGhost is unreachable. A 3.1.1 NEGOTIATE with a SMB2_COMPRESSION_CAPABILITIES negotiate context (MS-SMB2 2.2.3.1.3) advertising LZ77/LZ77+Huffman/LZNT1 and PATTERN_V1 that comes back with a mirrored context on Windows 10 1903/1909 identifies the pre-auth wormable SYSTEM RCE. Also enables the sibling CVE-2020-1206 SMBleed check.

missing_capabilities.name: Coerced-authentication reachability (PetitPotam / PrinterBug / DFSCoerce / MS-EFSR)
missing_capabilities.description: The signing-not-required finding tells operators about relay landing, but nothing tests whether the relay-source primitives are reachable. A null-session tree_connect to IPC$ and NamedPipeOpen against \PIPE\efsrpc (MS-EFSR 3.1.4 - PetitPotam), \PIPE\spoolss (MS-RPRN 3.1.4.1.9 - PrinterBug), \PIPE\netdfs (MS-DFSNM 3.1.4.1.1 - DFSCoerce), and \PIPE\lsarpc (MS-LSAD - CVE-2022-26925 PetitPotam-LSA) turns "could be relayed" into "here is the exact coercion primitive that answers unauthenticated". These are the standard chains and the module names them in narratives without ever probing them.

missing_capabilities.name: SMB2 native null-session tree_connect + SESSION_FLAGS parsing (IS_GUEST / IS_NULL)
missing_capabilities.description: Guest fallback and null fallback are detected only via nxc-parse output. MS-SMB2 2.2.6 SESSION_SETUP Response SessionFlags directly encodes SMB2_SESSION_FLAG_IS_GUEST (0x0001) and SMB2_SESSION_FLAG_IS_NULL (0x0002); sending a session_setup with garbage credentials and observing the returned SessionFlags is the canonical stdlib guest-fallback test ("any credential logs in as GUEST"). Currently the tool is a hard dependency for something the wire tells us for free.

missing_capabilities.name: SAMR / LSA / MS-SRVS null-session RPC enumeration (native)
missing_capabilities.description: The credfree layer emits an enum4linux-ng runbook step but does no RPC itself. Direct MS-SAMR (SamrConnect/SamrEnumerateDomainsInSamServer/SamrOpenDomain/SamrEnumerateUsersInDomain, 3.1.5), MS-LSAT (LsarLookupSids, 3.1.4), and MS-SRVS (NetrShareEnum, 3.1.4.8) calls over \PIPE\samr / \PIPE\lsarpc / \PIPE\srvsvc pull the domain SID, RID list, group memberships, share list, and session list credential-free on hosts where RestrictAnonymous!=1. This is also the primary feed for known_users and known_domains.

missing_capabilities.name: RID cycling (SamrLookupIdsInDomain 500..~1500)
missing_capabilities.description: Even without SamrEnumerateUsersInDomain, MS-SAMR SamrLookupIdsInDomain by RID (500=Administrator, 501=Guest, 502=krbtgt, 512=Domain Admins, then 1000+) returns the account name for each RID against many misconfigured hosts (esp. older Samba, and Windows with lsass anonymous restrictions off). Feeds known_users; the runbook mentions no equivalent primitive.

missing_capabilities.name: SMB3 encryption posture (SMB2_ENCRYPTION_CAPABILITIES)
missing_capabilities.description: Only the signing byte is inspected. On an SMB 3.x server the negotiate response's Capabilities.GLOBAL_CAP_ENCRYPTION and 3.1.1's SMB2_ENCRYPTION_CAPABILITIES context (AES-128-CCM/AES-128-GCM/AES-256-CCM/AES-256-GCM; MS-SMB2 2.2.3.1.2) determine whether the wire is confidentiality-protected. A 3.x server with encryption off is a hardening finding (and a plaintext-loot surface for man-in-the-middle plus SMB signing relay chains).

missing_capabilities.name: NTLMv1 downgrade detection (LMCompatibilityLevel < 3)
missing_capabilities.description: No probe determines whether the server accepts NTLMv1 responses. Sending a SESSION_SETUP with an NTLMSSP AUTHENTICATE using only NtChallengeResponse (24-byte NTLMv1) vs NTLMv2 blob and observing STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED vs STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE reveals LmCompatibilityLevel <= 2 -- crackable to plaintext with rainbow tables (~$20 crack.sh) and the trigger for MS-KILE downgrade attacks.

missing_capabilities.name: SambaCry / CVE-2017-7494 fingerprint
missing_capabilities.description: Writable-share proof already exists; combined with a Samba banner (from CHALLENGE Version 0/OS string on Samba, or nxc smb Samba-detection) it is one probe away from flagging CVE-2017-7494 (is_known_pipename() writable-share -> shared-object load -> unauth RCE against Samba 3.5.0-4.6.4/4.5.10/4.4.14).

missing_capabilities.name: CVE-2022-38023 / MS-NRPC signing bypass detection
missing_capabilities.description: Zerologon-era Netlogon RPC signing weakness. A NetrServerAuthenticate3 handshake test against \PIPE\netlogon (MS-NRPC 3.1.4.3) with signing disabled reveals the unpatched Netlogon RC4 / integrity-check bypass, and the same pipe surface still hosts CVE-2020-1472 Zerologon on missing August-2020 patches.

missing_capabilities.name: NetBIOS Name Service (UDP/137) nbstat
missing_capabilities.description: Recce hits TCP/445+139 only. A single UDP/137 NBSTAT query (RFC 1002 4.2.18) returns the workstation NetBIOS name, workgroup/domain, logged-on user (unique-name 03 record), and MAC address (statistics record) with no session and no TCP. Feeds known_hostnames/known_users/known_domains for the entire scan. Free and definitive on any pre-Windows-11-hardening host.

missing_capabilities.name: Named-pipe attack-surface enumeration on IPC$
missing_capabilities.description: Once a tree_connect to IPC$ succeeds (null or with creds), CREATE against \PIPE\svcctl (MS-SCMR service install -> RCE), \PIPE\atsvc (MS-TSCH scheduled task -> RCE), \PIPE\winreg (MS-RRP HKLM\SAM/SECURITY -> secretsdump precondition), \PIPE\eventlog, \PIPE\wkssvc all report reachable-or-not per principal. Each hit is either a lateral-movement primitive or a hash-dump precondition -- currently the module opens no named pipes at all.

missing_capabilities.name: Native MS17-010 tree_connect state-machine check
missing_capabilities.description: The finding today is "SMBv1 answered" and defers exploitability to an operator-run nmap NSE. The nmap check itself is a short SMBv1 TREE_CONNECT/TRANSACTION2 sequence testing STATUS_INSUFF_SERVER_RESOURCES vs STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED; porting it inline turns a maybe into a CONFIRMED CVE-2017-0143/0144 finding without shelling out.

missing_capabilities.name: SMB1 extended-negotiate ServerName/Domain/OS/Timezone/Encryption-Key harvest
missing_capabilities.description: The SMB1 probe returns only the boolean "answered". The extended SMB_COM_NEGOTIATE response also carries SecurityMode, EncryptionKey (challenge that reveals LMv1/NTLMv1 flow), ServerTime/TimeZone, and the trailing OEM/UNICODE ServerDomain\ServerName -- credential-free hostname/domain/time-skew intel from every host that still speaks SMBv1.

missing_capabilities.name: Preauth-integrity algorithm reporting (SMB2_PREAUTH_INTEGRITY_CAPABILITIES)
missing_capabilities.description: SMB 3.1.1's preauth-integrity context (MS-SMB2 2.2.3.1.1) reveals whether the server negotiates SHA-512, which gates downgrade-detection. Absent 3.1.1 offer entirely (the code path today), a scanner cannot report on preauth posture or the fixed dialect-downgrade class of attacks in the pre-3.1.1 era.

missing_capabilities.name: Kerberos ticket / SMB2 KerberosAP session_setup path
missing_capabilities.description: enum_session always uses NTLMSSP-in-SMB2. When the target is domain-joined and creds include a Kerberos ticket (KRB5CCNAME) or an AS-REP-roastable target is present, an AP-REQ session setup via GSS-Krb5 (RFC 4121; MS-SMB2 3.3.5.5) is the correct auth. Missing this path means Kerberos-only environments and pass-the-ticket workflows are invisible to this module.

missing_capabilities.name: SMB1-writable-share NTLM-coercion payload (.SCF / desktop.ini) auto-drop with Responder handoff
missing_capabilities.description: The writable-share narrative names the .SCF/.URL/.LNK/desktop.ini poisoned-icon primitive; the prove_writable path only drops recce_smb_probe.txt. A safe operator-opt-in "drop poisoned icon file pointing at <listener>" primitive turns the finding into a captured NetNTLMv2 hash feeding known_hashes -- and CVE-2024-43451 (NTLM hash disclosure via .URL) is an in-scope 2024 detection surface here.

missing_capabilities.name: SMB CVE roll (2022-24491/24500 uninit read/leak, 2023-21752 EFS EoP surface via SMB share, 2023-32233 Nftables not-SMB but 2023-23397 Outlook UNC coercion via SMB listener)
missing_capabilities.description: The module reports no SMB CVE beyond MS17-010. At minimum, banner/build derived from the CHALLENGE Version field can flag missing patch levels for CVE-2022-24491, CVE-2022-24500, CVE-2022-32230, CVE-2023-21752, and CVE-2024-26169-related surfaces without any additional traffic.

missing_capabilities.name: Password-policy extraction (SamrQueryInformationDomain) fed to spray planner
missing_capabilities.description: nxc --pass-pol output is captured but only rendered; the numeric MinPasswordLength/LockoutThreshold/LockoutDuration are not parsed into a structured object that a spray planner (owning the spray budget: attempts < LockoutThreshold-1 per window) can consume. This is what determines whether spray is safe -- the module surfaces the raw text and leaves it there.

missing_capabilities.name: Signing-required=True but Encryption=off distinction
missing_capabilities.description: The 'good' side of signing (SIGN_REQUIRED=True) is treated as clean, but on SMB 3.x a signed-yet-unencrypted session still exposes filenames, share names, and every read/write payload to a wire tap. An 'encryption disabled while signed' finding at low/medium is the right hardening surface -- currently invisible.

missing_capabilities.name: SMBv1 signing-required flag parsing
missing_capabilities.description: The SMB1 SecurityMode byte carries SIGNING_ENABLED (0x04) and SIGNING_REQUIRED (0x08) independently of the SMB2 posture. A dual-stack host can be SMB2-signing-required and still accept unsigned SMB1 (or vice versa on Samba) -- the module does not currently parse this from parse_smb1_negotiate.

priority_gaps: NTLMSSP CHALLENGE harvest via SESSION_SETUP -- one extra credfree round-trip yields NetBIOS name, DNS FQDN, AD domain/tree, OS build, server time; feeds known_hostnames/known_domains for the whole scan

Cross-service wiring: emit relay_targets (every signing_required=False host), known_users (SAMR), known_hostnames/known_domains (CHALLENGE + nbstat) so ldap/mssql/vsphere/vault/ntlmrelayx planning consumes SMB intel -- infrastructure exists in creds/known_users.py + core/known_domains.py and is currently unused by smb.py

CVE-2020-0796 SMBGhost detection: the deliberate 0x0311 avoidance closes off the only path to detecting SMBGhost and SMBleed; a properly-formed 3.1.1 NEGOTIATE with SMB2_COMPRESSION_CAPABILITIES/SMB2_PREAUTH_INTEGRITY_CAPABILITIES contexts is required

Coerced-auth primitive reachability: null-tree_connect + NamedPipeOpen against \PIPE\efsrpc, \PIPE\spoolss, \PIPE\netdfs, \PIPE\lsarpc to flag which of PetitPotam/PrinterBug/DFSCoerce/MS-EFSR-LSA actually answers unauth (converts the abstract relay narrative into a specific relay chain per host)
Native null-session SAMR/LSA/SRVS RPC enumeration (users, groups, SID, share list, sessions) instead of pure nxc dependency -- also the required feed for RID cycling and known_users
NBSTAT UDP/137 credfree name/user/MAC harvest -- the module ignores port 137 entirely; single-packet enrichment
MS17-010 native tree_connect state-machine check to promote 'SMBv1 answered' from surface finding to CONFIRMED CVE without shelling out to nmap NSE
NTLMv1 acceptance test (LMCompatibilityLevel <=2 crack.sh surface) via crafted SESSION_SETUP
SMB2 SESSION_SETUP SessionFlags parsing to detect guest-fallback (IS_GUEST 0x0001) natively without nxc
Password-policy structured extraction (MS-SAMR SamrQueryInformationDomain) so a spray planner can honor LockoutThreshold instead of the operator eyeballing raw --pass-pol text
cross_service_wire_gaps: known_hostnames: no feed from NTLMSSP CHALLENGE MsvAvNbComputerName/MsvAvDnsComputerName/MsvAvDnsTreeName or from NBSTAT unique-name records
known_domains: no feed from NTLMSSP CHALLENGE MsvAvNbDomainName/MsvAvDnsDomainName or SMB1 extended-negotiate ServerDomain -- core/known_domains.py already advertises SMB as its expected source
known_users: no feed from SAMR SamrEnumerateUsersInDomain / SamrLookupIdsInDomain (RID cycle) or from nxc --users parsed output; creds/known_users.py explicitly names SMB SAMR as the expected source

relay_targets: every signing_required=False host is a relay landing spot that ntlmrelayx (and the AD-CS/ESC8 chain) should consume -- mssql.py has relay_targets(); smb.py does not export one despite being the canonical producer
known_hashes: writable-share poisoned-icon (.SCF/.URL/desktop.ini) -> Responder capture flow is described in narratives but no automated hand-off populates known_hashes
machine_accounts / DC list: no export of ADMIN$/SYSVOL-observed DCs or DC-role signing_required=True hosts so downstream Kerberos/AD modules cannot key on them
server clock skew: NTLMSSP CHALLENGE MsvAvTimestamp gives the AD-authoritative time -- required for KRB5 skew tolerance in downstream Kerberoast/AS-REP paths and currently not harvested
notes: The module is deep on the two credfree postures it already covers (SMBv1-on and signing-not-required) and clean on the live layer (null->guest->creds ladder, reversible write proof, secret-file spidering), but it stops at NEGOTIATE and delegates almost everything richer to nxc/enum4linux-ng. The two highest-ROI gaps are (1) taking one more credfree round-trip -- SESSION_SETUP with an NTLMSSP NEGOTIATE -- to harvest the CHALLENGE AV_PAIR intel that every SMB server hands out for free, and (2) actually wiring the SMB module into the cross-service known_users / known_hostnames / known_domains / relay_targets surfaces that other modules (mssql/vault/vsphere/ipmi/telnet) already produce or consume. After that, SMBGhost (the deliberate 0x0311 exclusion), the coerced-auth pipe-reachability matrix (PetitPotam/PrinterBug/DFSCoerce), and native SAMR enumeration are the next tier.
summary: SMB module has strong credfree posture detection (SMBv1, signing SIGN_ENABLED vs SIGN_REQUIRED split) and a solid live layer (nxc-driven null/guest/creds ladder, reversible writable-share proof, share spidering), but it stops at SMB2 NEGOTIATE and does no SESSION_SETUP, no NTLMSSP CHALLENGE harvest, no coerced-auth pipe reachability, no native SAMR/LSA/SRVS RPC, no NBSTAT, no 3.1.1 negotiate contexts (so no SMBGhost / preauth-integrity / encryption posture), and does not feed known_users / known_hostnames / known_domains / relay_targets despite being the canonical producer named by those surfaces.
